terms.definition: The part of a plant that grows downward into the soil to anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals.
terms.function: Supplies the plant with water and minerals and holds it in place.
terms.whereItIs: Underground, extending down into the soil.
terms.whyItMatters: Without roots, plants could not stand up or get water and could not survive.

terms.definition: Tiny finger-like extensions on a root that greatly increase its surface area for absorbing water and minerals.
terms.function: Cause the root to soak up more water from the soil.
terms.whereItIs: Just behind the tip of the root.
terms.whyItMatters: More root hairs mean a healthy, well-watered plant.

terms.definition: A protective covering at the very tip of a root that shields the growing tip as it pushes through the soil.
terms.function: Protects the delicate tip from damage as the root grows downward.
terms.whereItIs: At the very tip of the root.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets the root safely grow through rough soil and stones.

terms.definition: Tiny tubes in the plant that carry water upward, from the root into the stem and leaves.
terms.function: Transports water and minerals up from the root.
terms.whereItIs: Running through the core of the root, up the stem.
terms.whyItMatters: It carries the water that roots take in up to the rest of the plant.
